notes.meaning: King Sargon of Assyria sent his supreme commander to attack and conquer the Philistine city of Ashdod. Ashdod had rebelled against Assyrian rule, hoping that Egypt would come to its rescue. The city's swift defeat showed everyone in the region that Assyria was an unstoppable world power.

God told Isaiah to remove his sandals and take off the rough sackcloth he wore as a prophet. Isaiah obeyed, walking around barefoot and stripped down to his light undergarment like a humble captive or slave. God gave His prophet this dramatic task so the message would catch the people's attention and warn them of coming judgment.

God explained the true meaning of Isaiah's strange appearance to the watching people. Walking stripped and barefoot served as a three-year sign of the disaster heading toward Egypt and Cush. God gave this living warning over an extended period so His people would have ample time to turn away from false alliances.

Assyria's armies would soon round up the people of Egypt and Cush and drive them into captivity. Young and old alike would be stripped of their clothes and marched away barefoot in total humiliation. The scene revealed how thoroughly the proud nations along the Nile would be disgraced.

All who pinned their hopes on Cush and bragged about Egypt's military might would be left terrified and ashamed. Many in Judah had looked to these southern superpowers for protection instead of seeking God. Putting our ultimate trust in human strength always leads to disappointment.

The people living along the coastal region would cry out in utter despair when they saw Egypt fall. They had counted on Egypt to protect them from the Assyrian war machine, only to see their protector collapse. If the mightiest world powers could not save themselves, smaller nations had no hope unless they trusted the Lord.
